notes.title: No more...
notes.notes: I'm sorry to the folks who have messaged me.  A while back 20,000 achievements were earned by the community and so Infinite Children is fully extended into its proper length and form.  There are no longer achievements to earn.  Those of you who made it happen - and earned your 50 achievements - are special.

notes.title: The Regression is over.
notes.notes: The Regression is over.  Once again, Infinite Children gets a little bit longer when anyone gets an achievement.  The original 50 achievements are once again available, if you hadn't already earned them this past summer.

notes.title: The Regression has begun
notes.notes:
There are 50 new achievements starting today.  Every time anyone earns a Steam achievement, the games gets shorter for everyone in the world.  

Think the story is too long and slow?  This is your chance to regress it down to just a handful of minutes long.

notes.title: The Regression begins July 8, 2019
notes.notes:
On July 8, [b]The Regression[/b] begins.  Every time anyone earns a steam achievement, the game will get a tiny bit shorter for everyone in the world.  Each community achievement will make Infinite Children a little less comprehensible, as The Regression subtracts story, images, sound, and, no doubt, time.  

After the 20,000th community achievement is earned, the Regression will be complete, manifesting as a ~7 minute version of the game - wholly frenetic and incoherent.  

There will be 50 new achievements available for The Regression, each entitled, “Regress This Game”.  The previous 50 that extended the game between May 6 and June 13 (which were entitled “Extend This Game”) will continue to not be available.

notes.title: Infinite Children is finally unlocked.
notes.notes:
A month ago, we released Infinite Children on Steam, but it was far too short! Today, @MarcusStewart7 unlocked the last achievement (20K) at @IndieCade #E3. Now that it is fully unlocked, please it play how it was meant to be - slow and steady.
